01.event: People ask Rabbi Elai where Rabbi Abbahu is hiding
01.turn: Elai answers in coded language that Abbahu consulted the Nasi and went south
01.outcome: Abbahu's whereabouts are revealed in riddle
01.summary: People ask Rabbi Elai where Rabbi Abbahu has gone. He answers in cryptic language that Abbahu took counsel with the Nasi and went south to the Sages there.
01.missing: Abbahu's departure is only reported in speech; nothing follows the exchange
01.reason: Mainly dialogue, but it reports a real event (Abbahu's departure after consulting the Nasi); mainly speech with an event mentioned is borderline.

02.missing: No single event; only Rava's habitual ruling practice
02.reason: A report of what Rava used to say to petitioners, a custom leading nowhere, with no one-time event.

03.summary: Rav came to Apsetaya and forbade climbing even stripped trees; the Gemara explains he was fencing in a lax place.
03.missing: No response or consequence; only a ruling cited as evidence
03.reason: An arrival plus a ruling cited as precedent, with nothing following; a bare report of what a rabbi did.

04.event: A woman came before Ameimar claiming a tenth of the estate
04.turn: Her brothers said they would pay her off in cash if they had it
04.summary: Rav Minyumi saw a woman come before Ameimar asking for a tenth of her father's estate. Her brothers said they would pay her in money if they could, and Ameimar said nothing, which shows he had changed his view.
04.missing: No action beyond coming to the rabbi and speech; no outcome for the woman
04.reason: A case brought before a rabbi where coming before him is the only event, followed by speech and silence used as legal evidence; under R-C0's limit this is not a story.

05.event: He betrothed a woman with a handful of onions from the field
05.outcome: Rava ruled the onions were stolen, so no betrothal
05.summary: A sharecropper betrothed a woman with a handful of onions taken from the field he worked. He came before Rava, who asked who had permitted him to take them, implying the betrothal was void.
05.missing: No change beyond the ruling; the rest is legal commentary
05.reason: There is a real act (taking and betrothing) and a ruling, close to the cow case, but it is essentially one event then a ruling; between borderline and not, choose borderline.

06.missing: Only a ruling or a reported act with no continuation
06.reason: A bare report of a permission, or of what Rav Zevid himself did, with no response or consequence.

07.actor: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Hanina
07.missing: Only a teaching and a reaction to it; nothing happens
07.reason: Laughing at a teaching is a reaction within scholarly discourse that leads nowhere; no story.

08.actor: A fox; those who weighed the turnip
08.event: A fox nested in a turnip
08.summary: A fox made its nest inside a turnip. People weighed the turnip and found it weighed sixty litra of Tzippori.
08.missing: No protagonist's change or causal development; cited as a wonder to support a teaching
08.reason: There are events (nesting, weighing, finding) but little causality or change, a one-line wonder cited as evidence; borderline rather than not.

09.event: Ravina held his orphaned nephew's wine and was taking his own wine to Sikhra
09.turn: He asked Rav Ashi whether to take the orphan's wine along
09.outcome: Rav Ashi told him to go
09.summary: Ravina was guardian of his nephew's wine and was taking his own wine to Sikhra to sell. He asked Rav Ashi whether he could take the orphan's wine too, and Rav Ashi told him to go.
09.missing: No action or change beyond asking and receiving a ruling
09.reason: A setting followed by a question and a ruling; coming before the rabbi is the only event, so under R-C0's limit and R-C2 it is not a story.

10.event: He set a conditional divorce for the New Moon of Adar
10.turn: When Adar came he claimed he had said Nisan
10.outcome: The Gemara discusses the legal consequence
10.summary: A man told witnesses his bill of divorce would take effect if he did not marry by the New Moon of Adar. When Adar came, he claimed he had said Nisan, and the Gemara analyzes the case.
10.missing: No action beyond speech; no resolution
10.reason: Only speech acts followed by legal analysis, with no narrated event or change; a legal case rather than a story.

11.missing: Only a question and an answer about textual readings
11.reason: A question put to the people of Judea and their answer, speech without conflict or event.

12.event: A bill of divorce from Anan bar Hiyya was found in Sura
12.turn: The Sages searched and found only one other man of that name, and witnesses said he was in Neharde'a that day
12.outcome: Abaye and Rava debate whether to be concerned
12.summary: A bill of divorce was found in Sura from Anan bar Hiyya of Neharde'a. The Sages searched from Sura to Neharde'a and found only one other man of that name, and witnesses testified he had been in Neharde'a that day. Abaye and Rava then dispute whether the bill is still suspect.
12.missing: No outcome for the parties; the case ends in legal debate
12.reason: There are real events (finding, investigation, testimony) but they lead only to a legal discussion with no narrated change; borderline.

13.actor: Rabbi Abba bar Shumni and Rav Menashya bar Yirmeya
13.event: Two scholars part at the ford of the Yofti River
13.turn: Each tells the other a halakha he has not heard
13.outcome: The teachings are recorded and discussed
13.summary: Two scholars taking leave of each other at a river ford agreed that each would say a teaching the other had not heard. One defined drunkenness, the other spoke about a convert's property; later sages add comments.
13.missing: No event beyond the parting setting; all content is teaching
13.reason: A setting that only frames teachings; teaching is speech, and with no conflict and no further event it is not a story.

14.event: His daughter asks whether he wants to sleep a little
14.turn: He answers that there will be long days for sleep after death
14.summary: Rav Hisda's daughter asked her father, who studied at night, whether he did not want to sleep a little. He replied that the long days of death would soon come, when he would sleep plenty.
14.missing: No action beyond speech; the habit of study is only implied
14.reason: A speech exchange without conflict or narrated event; under R-C2 speech without conflict is not a story.

15.event: He wished to give away his movable property
15.turn: Told he needed land, he acquired a small rock plot and gave it with sheep and barrels
15.outcome: He died, and the Sages carried out his words
15.summary: A Madonite in Jerusalem who was ill wanted to give his movable property as a gift. Told he could only do so by means of land, he bought a rocky plot near Jerusalem and gave it with a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels. He died, and the Sages carried out his gift.
15.reason: Several narrated actions with change (acquisition, death, fulfillment) ending in an outcome; an incident with legal resolution is a story under R-C0.

16.event: The exiles encamped by the Heker well
16.turn: The prophets permitted it, or it was ancestral custom
16.summary: When the exiles returned from Babylonia they camped by a certain well and were permitted to draw from it on a Festival.
16.missing: No development; a historical note supporting a ruling
16.reason: A bare historical report cited for a ruling, with no action leading anywhere.

17.actor: The people of Neharde'a; Rav Nahman
17.event: During a drought everyone sold their mansions to buy wheat
17.turn: Wheat then arrived and prices fell
17.outcome: Rav Nahman ruled the mansions return to their owners
17.summary: In a drought in Neharde'a, everyone sold their mansions to buy wheat. Then wheat arrived and the sales proved unnecessary, and Rav Nahman ruled that the mansions must be returned to their owners.
17.reason: A narrated incident with several actions and a change (drought, sales, arrival of wheat) resolved by a ruling, matching R-C0's cow case.

18.actor: Mar Yehuda, Rav Yosef, Rav Shmuel son of Rabba bar bar Hana, Rabba
18.event: Mar Yehuda finds the two at the study hall door and poses a contradiction
18.turn: They are silent and go before Rabba
18.outcome: Rabba says a quarrelsome person put them up to it and resolves the difficulty
18.summary: Mar Yehuda met two scholars at the entrance to Rabba's study hall and posed a contradiction in Rabbi Shimon's view. They could not answer and went to Rabba, who chided them that a quarrelsome man had set them up and resolved the difficulty.
18.missing: Events are mostly speech; the change is only being stumped and then answered
18.reason: Mainly scholarly dialogue, but with some movement (encounter, silence, going to Rabba) and a sharp rebuke; between not and borderline, choose borderline.

19.event: Rabbi Zeira avoided his teacher Rav Yehuda
19.turn: Because he wanted to go to Eretz Yisrael and Rav Yehuda forbade it
19.summary: Rabbi Zeira wanted to emigrate to Eretz Yisrael and kept avoiding his teacher Rav Yehuda, who held that leaving Babylonia violated a commandment.
19.missing: No one-time event or outcome within the passage
19.reason: A real ongoing action with conflict between student and teacher, but no event follows within the passage; borderline rather than not.

20.actor: A man who sold his mother's ketubah rights
20.event: He sold the rights, disclaiming liability if his mother objected
20.turn: His mother died without objecting, and he himself contested the sale
20.outcome: Rava ruled he guaranteed against his own objection
20.summary: A man sold his future rights to his mother's marriage contract, saying he would not reimburse the buyer if his mother objected. His mother died without objecting, and he himself came to contest the sale. Rami bar Hama thought he stood in her place, but Rava ruled he had guaranteed against his own claim.
20.reason: Several narrated events with change (sale, mother's death, his reversal) resolved by a ruling, matching R-C0's incident-plus-ruling shape.
